_about: Curated technique knowledge base. `documented_effect` summarises, qualitatively, what the cited source reports; no effect sizes are stated here unless the cited source states them. `requires` thresholds are screening heuristics written for this demo (rationale in `requires_basis`), not agronomic prescriptions. Every DOI and URL is checked by scripts/check_evidence.py (Crossref title match / HTTP status) and the result is shown next to the citation. Entries whose evidence_url is null have no verified link: the UI prints 'not available'. Aridity thresholds follow the UNEP (1992) classes: hyper-arid < 0.05, arid 0.05–0.20, semi-arid 0.20–0.50, dry sub-humid 0.50–0.65.

techniques.technique: Runoff agriculture with microcatchments and contour-bounded runoff plots
techniques.requires_basis: Runoff farming concentrates scarce rain from a bare catchment onto a cropped area: it only pays where rainfall alone cannot sustain the crop (arid to drier semi-arid), where there is some rain to harvest, and where the land has enough slope to generate runoff.
techniques.documented_effect: Describes rainwater-harvesting (runoff) agriculture, developed from ancient Negev runoff farms, as a way to produce food in arid zones where rainfall alone cannot support crops.
techniques.evidence_source: Bruins, H.J., Evenari, M. & Nessler, U. (1986). Rainwater-harvesting agriculture for food production in arid zones: the challenge of the African famine. Applied Geography 6(1): 13–32.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Catchment-to-cropped-area ratio must be sized to local rainfall and soil crusting; loess soils that crust generate runoff readily, sandy soils do not. Needs maintenance of bunds after every flood.

techniques.technique: Drip irrigation with brackish groundwater plus a leaching fraction
techniques.requires_basis: Using saline water safely depends on leaching salts below the root zone, which needs reasonably permeable soils (not heavy clay) and is only worth it where irrigation is essential.
techniques.documented_effect: FAO guidance on producing crops with saline water, covering crop salt tolerance, leaching requirements and irrigation methods; drip is described as favourable because it keeps the root zone continuously moist and salts pushed to the wetting-front margin.
techniques.evidence_source: Rhoades, J.D., Kandiah, A. & Mashali, A.M. (1992). The use of saline waters for crop production. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 48. Rome: FAO.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Measure irrigation-water EC and sodium (SAR) first; high-SAR water can disperse clay and seal the surface. Requires drainage for the leached salts and salt-tolerant crop choice.

techniques.technique: Limans: small runoff-fed tree groves in wadi depressions
techniques.requires_basis: Limans depend on seasonal flood runoff collected behind small earth dikes; they apply in arid lands with occasional runoff-producing storms and gently sloping drainage lines.
techniques.documented_effect: The Negev runoff-farming research programme at Avdat and Shivta documents ancient and reconstructed runoff farms, the basis for runoff-fed tree plantings.
techniques.evidence_source: Evenari, M., Shanan, L. & Tadmor, N. (1982). The Negev: The Challenge of a Desert, 2nd edition. Harvard University Press.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Dike height and spillway must match the expected flood volume; overtopping destroys the structure. Trees need establishment irrigation in the first seasons.

techniques.technique: Shade and photoselective netting over vegetables and orchards
techniques.requires_basis: Netting is used to cut radiation and heat load in hot, high-radiation summers; it offers little in cool or cloudy climates.
techniques.documented_effect: Introduces coloured, light-manipulating nets for fruit trees that change the spectral quality and amount of light reaching the crop in addition to physical protection.
techniques.evidence_source: Shahak, Y., Gussakovsky, E.E., Gal, E. & Ganelevin, R. (2004). ColorNets: crop protection and light-quality manipulation in one technology. Acta Horticulturae 659: 143–151.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Shade factor and colour must be chosen per crop; too much shade lowers yield. Structures must be rated for local wind loads.

techniques.technique: Drip fertigation: nutrients injected into drip water in small, frequent doses
techniques.requires_basis: Presumes an existing drip system, which is only standard where irrigation is required.
techniques.documented_effect: Handbook describing fertigation practice and its rationale: matching nutrient supply to crop uptake through the irrigation water.
techniques.evidence_source: Kafkafi, U. & Tarchitzky, J. (2011). Fertigation: A Tool for Efficient Fertilizer and Water Management. International Fertilizer Industry Association (IFA) and International Potash Institute (IPI), Paris.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs soluble fertilisers, a backflow preventer and filtration; phosphate and calcium can precipitate and clog emitters in hard water.

techniques.technique: Irrigation with treated wastewater blended with fresh water
techniques.requires_basis: Treated wastewater reuse is a response to severe freshwater scarcity; it is most relevant in arid and semi-arid basins.
techniques.documented_effect: FAO report on the economics of wastewater use in agriculture, including valuation of treated-wastewater reuse and case material from the Jordan Valley.
techniques.evidence_source: Winpenny, J., Heinz, I. & Koo-Oshima, S. (2010). The wealth of waste: The economics of wastewater use in agriculture. FAO Water Reports 35. Rome: FAO.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Requires treatment to the national/WHO standard for the target crop; restrict to crops not eaten raw unless water meets unrestricted-reuse quality. Monitor soil salinity and boron.

techniques.technique: Irrigation scheduling from evaporation-pan or weather-station ET and FAO-56 crop coefficients
techniques.requires_basis: Scheduling from reference ET matters where irrigation supplies most of the crop water.
techniques.documented_effect: FAO-56 defines the reference-evapotranspiration and crop-coefficient method for computing crop water requirements, including the pan-evaporation method.
techniques.evidence_source: Allen, R.G., Pereira, L.S., Raes, D. & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration — Guidelines for computing crop water requirements. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56. Rome: FAO.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Pan coefficients depend on pan siting and fetch; calibrate against local soil-moisture observations in the first season.

techniques.technique: Enarenado: a layer of sand over manure and imported soil under greenhouses
techniques.requires_basis: The sand mulch is a response to high evaporation and poor, saline native soils in a mild-winter arid coast; frost-prone climates cannot grow the winter greenhouse crops it supports.
techniques.documented_effect: Geographical account of the Almería horticulture industry, describing the enarenado sanded-soil system that underpins greenhouse vegetable production there.
techniques.evidence_source: Tout, D. (1990). The horticulture industry of Almería province, Spain. The Geographical Journal 156(3): 304–312.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Requires a source of clean coarse sand and manure; the system is labour-intensive to build and is normally combined with greenhouse cover and drip irrigation.

techniques.technique: Seasonal whitewashing (calcium carbonate) of greenhouse plastic
techniques.requires_basis: Whitewashing reflects summer radiation to limit heat inside greenhouses; it is a hot-season measure.
techniques.documented_effect: Reports a regional surface cooling trend in Almería attributed to the high reflectivity (albedo) of the greenhouse area, in which summer whitewashing of roofs plays a part.
techniques.evidence_source: Campra, P., Garcia, M., Canton, Y. & Palacios-Orueta, A. (2008). Surface temperature cooling trends and negative radiative forcing due to land use change toward greenhouse farming in southeastern Spain. Journal of Geophysical Research 113: D18109.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Coating must be washed off before the low-light season. Only relevant where greenhouses are already in use.

techniques.technique: Soil-moisture sensor and tensiometer scheduling of drip fertigation to limit nitrate leaching
techniques.requires_basis: Relevant where crops are drip-irrigated and over-irrigation carries nitrate below the root zone.
techniques.documented_effect: Survey of greenhouse farms in Almería identifying the irrigation and nitrogen practices that contribute to nitrate leaching, which motivates sensor-based scheduling.
techniques.evidence_source: Thompson, R.B., Martínez-Gaitán, C., Gallardo, M., Giménez, C. & Fernández, M.D. (2007). Identification of irrigation and N management practices that contribute to nitrate leaching loss from an intensive vegetable production system by use of a comprehensive survey. Agricultural Water Management 89: 261–274.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Tensiometers need servicing and fail in very dry or very saline soils; install at two depths per irrigation sector.

techniques.technique: Low-cost 'parral' plastic greenhouses with passive ventilation
techniques.requires_basis: Unheated parral greenhouses depend on mild winters for off-season production; frost-prone climates need heated structures.
techniques.documented_effect: Techno-economic analysis of Almería greenhouse agriculture describing the parral structure, its costs and its role in the region's horticulture.
techniques.evidence_source: Valera, D.L., Belmonte, L.J., Molina-Aiz, F.D. & López, A. (2016). Greenhouse agriculture in Almería: a comprehensive techno-economic analysis. Cajamar Caja Rural, Serie Economía.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs design for local wind loads and hail; passive ventilation is insufficient in humid tropical climates without additional cooling.

techniques.technique: Regulated deficit irrigation (RDI) in fruit trees and vines
techniques.requires_basis: RDI withholds water in drought-tolerant phenological stages; it presumes irrigation control, i.e. irrigation-dependent climates.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews Spanish research on deficit irrigation in fruit trees and vines, including which growth stages tolerate water deficit and the resulting water savings and fruit-quality effects.
techniques.evidence_source: Ruiz-Sánchez, M.C., Domingo, R. & Castel, J.R. (2010). Review. Deficit irrigation in fruit trees and vines in Spain. Spanish Journal of Agricultural Research 8(S2): S5–S20.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Stress-sensitive stages differ by species and cultivar; RDI needs monitoring (stem water potential or soil moisture) to avoid yield loss.

techniques.technique: Irrigation with desalinated seawater blended with other sources
techniques.requires_basis: Desalinated water is costly to produce and pump uphill; it is used in severely water-short areas near the coast.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews current experience of using desalinated seawater for irrigation, including south-east Spain, and the key issues: cost, energy, and boron and nutrient imbalances in the product water.
techniques.evidence_source: Martínez-Alvarez, V., Martin-Gorriz, B. & Soto-García, M. (2016). Seawater desalination for crop irrigation — a review of current experiences and revealed key issues. Desalination 381: 58–70.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Desalinated water can lack Ca and Mg and carry boron; blending or remineralisation is usually needed. Only viable with an existing desalination plant.

techniques.technique: Suspended shade covers on on-farm irrigation reservoirs to reduce evaporation
techniques.requires_basis: Open-water evaporation losses matter most in hot, arid climates where stored irrigation water is scarce.
techniques.documented_effect: Measures how effectively different shading materials reduce evaporation from free water surfaces, for application to agricultural reservoirs.
techniques.evidence_source: Martínez Alvarez, V., Baille, A., Molina Martínez, J.M. & González-Real, M.M. (2006). Efficiency of shading materials in reducing evaporation from free water surfaces. Agricultural Water Management 84: 229–239.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Only useful where water is stored in open ponds; cover structures must withstand local wind.

techniques.technique: Anti-hail netting over vineyards and orchards
techniques.requires_basis: Screening heuristic: hail netting in the source region protects temperate fruit and vines; the rule restricts it to temperate climates where those crops are grown.
techniques.documented_effect: not available (no verified source linked for this entry)
techniques.evidence_source: INTA EEA Mendoza extension material on hail protection (no specific trial report linked).
techniques.adaptation_notes: Only justified where hail frequency is high; netting also shades the crop, which can delay ripening.

techniques.technique: Controlled deficit irrigation in red wine grapes
techniques.requires_basis: Deficit irrigation in vines needs irrigation control (arid climate) and applies to temperate wine-grape regions.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews physiological and molecular evidence on grapevine responses to deficit irrigation, including effects on vigour, water-use efficiency and berry quality.
techniques.evidence_source: Chaves, M.M., Zarrouk, O., Francisco, R., Costa, J.M., Santos, T., Regalado, A.P., Rodrigues, M.L. & Lopes, C.M. (2010). Grapevine under deficit irrigation: hints from physiological and molecular data. Annals of Botany 105: 661–676.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Evidence is largely from Mediterranean-climate vineyards; timing must be adjusted to local phenology and to the cultivar.

techniques.technique: Inter-row cover crops in irrigated vineyards
techniques.requires_basis: Cover crops compete for water; in the source region they are grown under irrigation. Steep slopes need different erosion measures.
techniques.documented_effect: not available (no verified source linked for this entry)
techniques.evidence_source: INTA EEA Mendoza extension material on vineyard cover crops (no specific trial report linked).
techniques.adaptation_notes: Choose species and mowing dates so cover-crop water use does not coincide with critical vine stages.

techniques.technique: Conversion of furrow-irrigated vineyards to pressurised drip
techniques.requires_basis: The source region is arid and fully irrigation-dependent; the rule keeps the technique to arid climates.
techniques.documented_effect: not available (no verified source linked for this entry)
techniques.evidence_source: INTA EEA San Juan extension material (no specific trial report linked).
techniques.adaptation_notes: Requires reliable pressure (pump or elevation head) and filtration of canal water with high sediment load.

techniques.technique: Tree windbreaks (e.g. poplar rows) around irrigated plots
techniques.requires_basis: Windbreaks work best on open, gently sloping land; on steep ground topography dominates wind flow.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews windbreak research in North American agriculture: reduced wind speed in the sheltered zone, microclimate changes and crop and soil-erosion effects.
techniques.evidence_source: Brandle, J.R., Hodges, L. & Zhou, X.H. (2004). Windbreaks in North American agricultural systems. Agroforestry Systems 61: 65–78.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Evidence is from North America; windbreak trees need water themselves in arid areas and shade the rows next to them.

techniques.technique: Subsurface drip irrigation (SDI) of row crops
techniques.requires_basis: Irrigation-dependent climates (UNEP drylands, AI < 0.65); very coarse sands limit lateral wetting from buried emitters.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews 15 years of subsurface drip research on row crops at the USDA-ARS Water Management Research Laboratory (Fresno), including yield, water use and salinity management.
techniques.evidence_source: Ayars, J.E., Phene, C.J., Hutmacher, R.B., Davis, K.R., Schoneman, R.A., Vail, S.S. & Mead, R.M. (1999). Subsurface drip irrigation of row crops: a review of 15 years of research at the Water Management Research Laboratory. Agricultural Water Management 42: 1–27.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Requires filtration and acid/chlorine maintenance; rodent damage and root intrusion are the common failure modes.

techniques.technique: Winter cover crops combined with no-till in irrigated annual crops
techniques.requires_basis: A winter cover crop needs some winter rain (or irrigation) and winters mild enough for it to grow.
techniques.documented_effect: Long-term trial in the San Joaquin Valley reporting that cover cropping and no-tillage improved soil-health indicators in an arid irrigated system.
techniques.evidence_source: Mitchell, J.P. et al. (2017). Cover cropping and no-tillage improve soil health in an arid irrigated cropping system in California's San Joaquin Valley, USA. Soil & Tillage Research 165: 325–335.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs no-till planting equipment; cover crop must be terminated early enough not to deplete stored soil water.

techniques.technique: Gypsum application to improve infiltration in sodic or low-salinity-water-sealed soils
techniques.requires_basis: Gypsum addresses sodium-induced clay dispersion and surface sealing, which occur in neutral-to-alkaline soils with meaningful clay content.
techniques.documented_effect: FAO guidance on irrigation-water quality, including infiltration problems caused by sodium or very low-salinity water and their correction with gypsum amendments.
techniques.evidence_source: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. Rome: FAO.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Confirm sodicity (ESP/SAR) with a lab test before applying; gypsum does nothing for non-sodic compaction.

techniques.technique: On-farm winter flood recharge (Flood-MAR) of groundwater on dormant fields
techniques.requires_basis: Recharge by flooding needs permeable soils, flat fields and a strongly seasonal climate that produces surplus winter flows.
techniques.documented_effect: Field experiments reporting that managed winter flooding of alfalfa recharged groundwater with minimal crop damage.
techniques.evidence_source: Dahlke, H.E., Brown, A.G., Orloff, S., Putnam, D. & O'Geen, T. (2018). Managed winter flooding of alfalfa recharges groundwater with minimal crop damage. California Agriculture 72(1): 65–75.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs access to surplus surface water and a legal framework for recharge; avoid fields with nitrate legacies that would be flushed to the aquifer.

techniques.technique: Midday stem water potential (pressure chamber) to schedule orchard irrigation
techniques.requires_basis: Plant-based scheduling is used in irrigated orchards in dry climates.
techniques.documented_effect: Establishes plant water status (stem water potential) as an index of irrigation need in deciduous fruit trees.
techniques.evidence_source: Shackel, K.A. et al. (1997). Plant water status as an index of irrigation need in deciduous fruit trees. HortTechnology 7(1): 23–29.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Baseline values are species-specific; readings must be taken at midday on bagged, shaded leaves.

techniques.technique: Optical-sensor (NDVI) based nitrogen top-dressing in irrigated wheat
techniques.requires_basis: Tested in fully irrigated wheat, where nitrogen rather than water limits yield.
techniques.documented_effect: Reports reduced nitrogen use and improved farm income in irrigated spring wheat in the Yaqui Valley using sensor-based nitrogen management.
techniques.evidence_source: Ortiz-Monasterio, J.I. & Raun, W. (2007). Reduced nitrogen and improved farm income for irrigated spring wheat in the Yaqui Valley, Mexico, using sensor based nitrogen management. Journal of Agricultural Science 145: 215–222.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs an N-rich reference strip in each field; algorithms are calibrated per crop and region.

techniques.technique: Permanent raised beds with crop-residue retention under furrow irrigation
techniques.requires_basis: Furrow-irrigated beds need flat land and soils that hold a furrow.
techniques.documented_effect: Long-term trial in the Yaqui Valley comparing tillage and residue management on beds; reports effects on soil quality indicators.
techniques.evidence_source: Verhulst, N. et al. (2011). Soil quality as affected by tillage-residue management in a wheat-maize irrigated bed planting system. Plant and Soil 340: 453–466.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Requires bed-shaping and residue-tolerant planters; residue must be managed so it doesn't block furrows.

techniques.technique: Bed planting of irrigated wheat (furrow-irrigated raised beds)
techniques.requires_basis: Furrow irrigation between beds needs flat fields and an irrigation-dependent climate.
techniques.documented_effect: Trial of straw management and nitrogen rates in a bed-planting system reporting wheat and maize yield responses.
techniques.evidence_source: Limon-Ortega, A., Sayre, K.D. & Francis, C.A. (2000). Wheat and maize yields in response to straw management and nitrogen under a bed planting system. Agronomy Journal 92: 295–302.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Row spacing and bed width must match available machinery.

techniques.technique: Underground (subsurface) dams across alluvial valley floors
techniques.requires_basis: Underground dams store rainy-season flow in valley sediments for the dry season; they suit semi-arid, strongly seasonal climates.
techniques.documented_effect: Uses ground-penetrating radar and 3D modelling to judge whether sites in a Brazilian semiarid sub-watershed are adequate for underground dams. It is a siting method and does not quantify crop effects.
techniques.evidence_source: Lima, A. de O., Lima-Filho, F.P., Dias, N. da S., Reis Júnior, J.A. dos & Sousa, A. de M. (2018). GPR 3D profile of the adequateness of underground dams in a sub-watershed of the Brazilian semiarid. Revista Caatinga 31: 523–531.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs an alluvial deposit over shallow impermeable bedrock; siting requires a simple survey of sediment depth.

techniques.technique: Rainwater cisterns for household and small-plot production (P1MC / P1+2 programmes)
techniques.requires_basis: Cisterns bridge a long dry season with rain stored in the wet season; they need enough rainfall to fill.
techniques.documented_effect: Viability assessment of the One Million Cisterns Programme as community rainwater management in Brazil's semiarid region.
techniques.evidence_source: Cardoso Castro, P.P., Vachkova, M., Ravena, N. & Veloso, N. (2024). The One Million Cisterns Programme — a viability assessment of community rainwater management in Brazil. Frontiers in Sustainability 5.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Storage volume must be sized to dry-season length and use; first-flush diversion protects water quality.

techniques.technique: Drip and micro-sprinkler irrigated tropical fruit (mango, grape) with scheduled irrigation cut-off
techniques.requires_basis: Tropical fruit needs frost-free warm winters; irrigated production suits semi-arid climates with reliable river water.
techniques.documented_effect: not available (no verified source linked for this entry)
techniques.evidence_source: Embrapa Semiárido irrigated-fruit research (no specific trial report linked).
techniques.adaptation_notes: Depends on a reliable perennial water source (the São Francisco river in the source region) and export market access.

techniques.technique: Khadin: runoff from a rocky catchment impounded behind an earthen bund, then cropped on residual moisture
techniques.requires_basis: Khadins need a runoff-producing catchment above a flat valley bottom in an arid climate.
techniques.documented_effect: Describes the khadin system of harvesting runoff water for agriculture in the Thar desert.
techniques.evidence_source: Kolarkar, A.S., Murthy, K.N.K. & Singh, N. (1983). Khadin — a method of harvesting water for agriculture in the Thar desert. Journal of Arid Environments 6: 59–66.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Salt accumulation can occur in the impounded bed if drainage is poor; bund spillways must pass large floods.

techniques.technique: Tanka / kund: covered underground cisterns fed by a prepared catchment
techniques.requires_basis: Cisterns suit arid areas with no reliable groundwater and some rain to collect.
techniques.documented_effect: Survey of India's traditional water-harvesting systems, including the tankas and kunds of the Thar desert.
techniques.evidence_source: Agarwal, A. & Narain, S. (eds.) (1997). Dying Wisdom: Rise, Fall and Potential of India's Traditional Water Harvesting Systems. Centre for Science and Environment, New Delhi.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Catchment surface must be kept clean; lining quality determines losses.

techniques.technique: Prosopis cineraria (khejri) parkland agroforestry with arable crops
techniques.requires_basis: Khejri is a deep-rooted arid-zone tree that tolerates heat and drought but not hard frost.
techniques.documented_effect: Studies how tree density affects the productivity of a Prosopis cineraria agroforestry system in north-western India.
techniques.evidence_source: Singh, G., Mutha, S. & Bala, N. (2007). Effect of tree density on productivity of a Prosopis cineraria agroforestry system in North Western India. Journal of Arid Environments 70: 152–163.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Prosopis cineraria is native to the Thar; do not substitute invasive Prosopis juliflora. Lopping regime controls competition with crops.

techniques.technique: Shelterbelts of drought-hardy trees against wind erosion and sand movement
techniques.requires_basis: Wind erosion is the main hazard on sandy soils in arid and semi-arid climates.
techniques.documented_effect: Measures soil drying and wind erosion behind different types of shelterbelts in the desert region of western Rajasthan.
techniques.evidence_source: Gupta, J.P., Rao, G.G.S.N., Gupta, G.N. & Ramana Rao, B.V. (1983). Soil drying and wind erosion as affected by different types of shelterbelts planted in the desert region of Western Rajasthan, India. Journal of Arid Environments 6: 53–58.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Establishment needs protection from grazing and a few seasons of watering.

techniques.technique: Pearl millet – legume (cluster bean, moth bean) rotation and intercropping
techniques.requires_basis: A rainfed arid-zone rotation; needs at least a short monsoon season.
techniques.documented_effect: not available (no verified source linked for this entry)
techniques.evidence_source: ICAR-Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI), Jodhpur — arid cropping-systems research.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Legume choice must match season length; guar (cluster bean) doubles as a cash crop.

techniques.technique: Community check dams and well recharge (Saurashtra recharge movement)
techniques.requires_basis: Recharge structures capture monsoon runoff for dry-season groundwater use; they need a short intense rainy season and an aquifer that can store it.
techniques.documented_effect: Analyses the farmer-led groundwater recharge movement in western India (Saurashtra), how it spread and what it achieved.
techniques.evidence_source: Shah, T. (2000). Mobilising social energy against environmental challenge: understanding the groundwater recharge movement in western India. Natural Resources Forum 24: 197–209.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Works where hard-rock or alluvial aquifers accept recharge; needs community coordination along the drainage line.

techniques.technique: Subsidised drip and sprinkler irrigation for smallholder cash crops
techniques.requires_basis: Micro-irrigation saves water where dry-season irrigation depends on scarce groundwater.
techniques.documented_effect: Empirical study of the economics, adoption determinants and impacts of micro-irrigation technologies in India.
techniques.evidence_source: Namara, R.E., Nagar, R.K. & Upadhyay, B. (2007). Economics, adoption determinants, and impacts of micro-irrigation technologies: empirical results from India. Irrigation Science 25: 283–297.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Adoption in the source region was supported by a state subsidy scheme; without one, capital cost is the main barrier.

techniques.technique: Tidal regulators, spreading channels and recharge to halt seawater ingress into coastal aquifers
techniques.requires_basis: Seawater intrusion is a problem of low-lying coastal aquifers.
techniques.documented_effect: not available (no verified source linked for this entry)
techniques.evidence_source: Gujarat Coastal Salinity Prevention Cell programme material (no specific evaluation linked).
techniques.adaptation_notes: Only relevant near a coast with pumping-induced intrusion; needs basin-scale planning.

techniques.technique: Drip irrigation under plastic film mulch for cotton
techniques.requires_basis: Film mulch in the source region warms soil in a short, cold-winter continental arid season and cuts evaporation; the rule keeps it to arid climates with cold winters.
techniques.documented_effect: Field study of the soil water and salt balance and the water productivity of typical irrigation schedules for film-mulched, drip-irrigated cotton in northern Xinjiang.
techniques.evidence_source: Ning, S., Zhou, B., Shi, J. & Wang, Q. (2021). Soil water/salt balance and water productivity of typical irrigation schedules for cotton under film mulched drip irrigation in northern Xinjiang. Agricultural Water Management 245: 106651.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Residual plastic film pollutes soils unless recovered; salt accumulates between drip lines and needs periodic leaching.

techniques.technique: Pre-season (winter or spring) flood leaching of accumulated salts
techniques.requires_basis: Leaching is needed where evaporation concentrates salts (arid) and is only effective where soils drain.
techniques.documented_effect: FAO guidance on salinity management describes leaching requirements and practices for removing salts from the root zone.
techniques.evidence_source: Rhoades, J.D., Kandiah, A. & Mashali, A.M. (1992). The use of saline waters for crop production. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 48. Rome: FAO.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Without drainage, leaching raises the water table and can worsen salinity. Uses large water volumes.

techniques.technique: Oasis farmland shelterbelt networks
techniques.requires_basis: Shelterbelt grids protect irrigated oases on open, flat land in arid, windy climates.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews windbreak research: reduced wind speed in the sheltered zone, microclimate changes and effects on crops and erosion.
techniques.evidence_source: Brandle, J.R., Hodges, L. & Zhou, X.H. (2004). Windbreaks in North American agricultural systems. Agroforestry Systems 61: 65–78.
techniques.adaptation_notes: The cited review is North American; shelterbelt trees need an irrigation allocation in oases.

techniques.technique: Alternate partial root-zone irrigation (PRD)
techniques.requires_basis: PRD is a water-saving irrigation regime; relevant where irrigation water is scarce.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews the physiology of controlled alternate partial root-zone irrigation and its effect on water-use efficiency.
techniques.evidence_source: Kang, S. & Zhang, J. (2004). Controlled alternate partial root-zone irrigation: its physiological consequences and impact on water use efficiency. Journal of Experimental Botany 55: 2437–2446.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs alternating furrows or dual drip lines and disciplined switching; the benefit is small on shallow soils.

techniques.technique: Sand dams across seasonal sandy riverbeds
techniques.requires_basis: Sand dams store wet-season flow in accumulated sand for the dry season; they need seasonal rivers in semi-arid, strongly seasonal climates.
techniques.documented_effect: Assesses the potential of community-built sand dams in Kitui, Kenya, for adaptation to droughts, including effects on water availability.
techniques.evidence_source: Lasage, R., Aerts, J., Mutiso, G.-C.M. & de Vries, A. (2008). Potential for community based adaptation to droughts: Sand dams in Kitui, Kenya. Physics and Chemistry of the Earth 33: 67–73.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs a sandy seasonal riverbed with bedrock close to the surface; a site survey is essential.

techniques.technique: Fanya juu terraces (soil thrown uphill to build bench terraces over time)
techniques.requires_basis: Terracing controls runoff and erosion on sloping cropland; it is not needed on flat land and becomes impractical on very steep slopes.
techniques.documented_effect: Long-term assessment in south-eastern Kenya of how fanya juu terraces affect soil organic matter on cultivated land.
techniques.evidence_source: Saiz, G., Wandera, F.M., Pelster, D.E., Ngetich, W., Okalebo, J.R., Rufino, M.C. & Butterbach-Bahl, K. (2016). Long-term assessment of soil and water conservation measures (Fanya-juu terraces) on soil organic matter in South Eastern Kenya. Geoderma 274: 1–9.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Labour-intensive to build; grass strips (e.g. Napier) on risers stabilise them and supply fodder.

techniques.technique: Conservation farming: ripping/sub-soiling with mulch retention in rainfed maize
techniques.requires_basis: Tested in semi-arid and dry sub-humid rainfed systems where rain-water capture limits yield.
techniques.documented_effect: On-farm action research in East and Southern Africa reporting yields and rain-water productivity under conservation farming compared with conventional tillage.
techniques.evidence_source: Rockström, J. et al. (2009). Conservation farming strategies in East and Southern Africa: Yields and rain water productivity from on-farm action research. Soil & Tillage Research 103: 23–32.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Mulch competes with livestock feed; rippers need draught power or a service provider.

techniques.technique: Maize – pigeonpea intercropping
techniques.requires_basis: Pigeonpea is a drought-tolerant, frost-sensitive legume of the semi-arid tropics.
techniques.documented_effect: Study of nitrogen use in maize–pigeonpea intercrops under semi-arid conditions in Kenya.
techniques.evidence_source: Wanderi, S.W., Mburu, M.W.K., Silim, S.N. & Kihanda, F.M. (2011). Nitrogen Use in Maize (Zea mays)–Pigeonpea (Cajanus cajans) Intercrop in Semi-arid Conditions of Kenya. In: Innovations as Key to the Green Revolution in Africa, pp. 563–570. Springer.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Choose pigeonpea maturity group to match rainfall season length.

techniques.technique: Zaï planting pits with manure on crusted, degraded land
techniques.requires_basis: Zaï pits concentrate rain and nutrients in the planting hole; they are used in semi-arid rainfed zones (roughly 300–800 mm) on crusted soils.
techniques.documented_effect: Case study from Burkina Faso of zaï as a traditional practice for rehabilitating semi-arid degraded land.
techniques.evidence_source: Roose, E., Kabore, V. & Guenat, C. (1999). Zaï practice: a West African traditional rehabilitation system for semiarid degraded lands, a case study in Burkina Faso. Arid Soil Research and Rehabilitation 13(4): 343–355.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Labour-intensive (digging in the dry season); needs a manure or compost supply. Termite activity in the pits helps restore infiltration.

techniques.technique: Half-moons (demi-lunes) with nutrient amendments
techniques.requires_basis: Half-moon bunds capture sheet runoff on gentle slopes in semi-arid zones.
techniques.documented_effect: Reports that the success of the half-moon practice in semi-arid Burkina Faso depended on combining it with nutrient amendments.
techniques.evidence_source: Zougmoré, R., Zida, Z. & Kambou, N.F. (2003). Role of nutrient amendments in the success of half-moon soil and water conservation practice in semiarid Burkina Faso. Soil & Tillage Research 71: 143–149.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs layout along contours; not effective on flat land where there is no runoff to capture.

techniques.technique: Contour stone bunds (cordons pierreux)
techniques.requires_basis: Stone bunds slow runoff on gently sloping fields in semi-arid zones; flat land generates little runoff.
techniques.documented_effect: Evaluates the effect of adopting stone lines and fertilizer micro-dosing on sorghum yield and income of smallholder farmers in Burkina Faso.
techniques.evidence_source: Sawadogo, D., Matsumura, I., Yasunobu, K., Fernandez, C. & Baya, A.E. (2023). Evaluation of the Effect of Stone Lines and Microdosing Adoption on Sorghum Yield and Income: A Case of Smallholder Farmers in Burkina Faso. Journal of Agricultural Science 15(6): 41.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs a local stone source and transport; bunds must follow contours laid out with a water-tube level.

techniques.technique: Farmer-managed natural regeneration (FMNR) of trees in cropland
techniques.requires_basis: FMNR regrows trees from living stumps in dryland cropland; documented in semi-arid to dry sub-humid Africa.
techniques.documented_effect: Makes the case for 'evergreen agriculture' — integrating trees such as Faidherbia albida and regenerated trees into annual cropping — drawing on experience from Niger and elsewhere in Africa.
techniques.evidence_source: Garrity, D.P. et al. (2010). Evergreen Agriculture: a robust approach to sustainable food security in Africa. Food Security 2: 197–214.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs living root stock in the soil and local agreements (tree tenure) so farmers benefit from protecting trees.

techniques.technique: Faidherbia albida parklands (trees that leaf out in the dry season)
techniques.requires_basis: Faidherbia is a tropical dryland tree, not frost-hardy.
techniques.documented_effect: Describes Faidherbia albida's reverse phenology and its use in evergreen-agriculture systems across Africa.
techniques.evidence_source: Garrity, D.P. et al. (2010). Evergreen Agriculture: a robust approach to sustainable food security in Africa. Food Security 2: 197–214.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Slow to establish; seedlings need protection from browsing for several years.

techniques.technique: Fertilizer micro-dosing (small doses placed in the planting hole)
techniques.requires_basis: Micro-dosing targets nutrient-poor soils (low organic carbon) in rainfed drylands.
techniques.documented_effect: Broad-scale on-farm trials presented as evidence for micro-dosing as a pathway to raising smallholder cereal yields.
techniques.evidence_source: Twomlow, S. et al. (2010). Micro-dosing as a pathway to Africa's Green Revolution: evidence from broad-scale on-farm trials. Nutrient Cycling in Agroecosystems 88: 3–15.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs fertiliser available in small, affordable packs and a measuring cap or bottle top for dose placement.

techniques.technique: Tree windbreaks against wind erosion on sandy Sahelian fields (e.g. Majjia Valley, Niger)
techniques.requires_basis: Wind erosion is the main hazard on sandy dryland soils.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews windbreak research: reduced wind speed in the sheltered zone, microclimate changes and effects on crops and erosion.
techniques.evidence_source: Brandle, J.R., Hodges, L. & Zhou, X.H. (2004). Windbreaks in North American agricultural systems. Agroforestry Systems 61: 65–78.
techniques.adaptation_notes: The cited review is North American; Sahelian windbreaks need grazing protection and species suited to low rainfall (e.g. neem was used in Majjia).

techniques.technique: Pearl millet – cowpea / groundnut rotation on sandy soils
techniques.requires_basis: Tested on sandy soils of the semi-arid West African tropics.
techniques.documented_effect: Field study of rotation and nitrogen fertiliser effects on pearl millet, cowpea and groundnut yields and soil chemical properties on a sandy soil in the semi-arid tropics of West Africa.
techniques.evidence_source: Bationo, A. & Ntare, B.R. (2000). Rotation and nitrogen fertilizer effects on pearl millet, cowpea and groundnut yield and soil chemical properties in a sandy soil in the semi-arid tropics, West Africa. Journal of Agricultural Science 134: 277–284.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Legume yields depend on phosphorus; combine with P micro-dosing on very poor soils.

techniques.technique: No-till seeding with full stubble retention
techniques.requires_basis: Adopted widely in rainfed grain regions from semi-arid to dry sub-humid, where conserving stored soil water drives yield.
techniques.documented_effect: Documents the extensive use of no-tillage in grain-growing regions of Australia and the factors behind adoption.
techniques.evidence_source: Llewellyn, R.S., D'Emden, F.H. & Kuehne, G. (2012). Extensive use of no-tillage in grain growing regions of Australia. Field Crops Research 132: 204–212.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Relies on herbicide weed control, which risks resistance; needs disc or tine seeders that handle residue.

techniques.technique: Break-crop rotations (canola, pulses) in wheat sequences
techniques.requires_basis: Break crops in the source region are winter crops in temperate, winter-rainfall or cool-season grain systems.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews break-crop benefits to following wheat crops in temperate production systems, including disease, nitrogen and water effects.
techniques.evidence_source: Kirkegaard, J., Christen, O., Krupinsky, J. & Layzell, D. (2008). Break crop benefits in temperate wheat production. Field Crops Research 107: 185–195.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Break-crop profitability depends on local prices; pulses need inoculant where they have not been grown before.

techniques.technique: Clay spreading and delving on water-repellent sandy soils
techniques.requires_basis: Only relevant on sands (typically non-wetting) with clay available in the subsoil or nearby.
techniques.documented_effect: Describes clay spreading on water-repellent sands in south-east South Australia as a sustainable-agriculture practice.
techniques.evidence_source: Cann, M.A. (2000). Clay spreading on water repellent sands in the south east of South Australia — promoting sustainable agriculture. Journal of Hydrology 231–232: 333–341.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Needs a clay source within economic distance or a clay layer reachable by delving; test clay for sodicity and boron first.

techniques.technique: Yield mapping and variable-rate fertiliser by management zone
techniques.requires_basis: Needs mechanised harvest with a yield monitor; works on broadacre fields.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews the status, issues and prospects of variable-rate fertiliser adoption in the Australian grains industry.
techniques.evidence_source: Robertson, M.J., Llewellyn, R.S., Mandel, R., Lawes, R., Bramley, R.G.V., Swift, L., Metz, N. & O'Callaghan, C. (2012). Adoption of variable rate fertiliser application in the Australian grains industry: status, issues and prospects. Precision Agriculture 13: 181–199.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Zones should be checked against soil tests; free satellite NDVI can substitute for yield maps in the first seasons.

techniques.technique: Fog collectors (atrapanieblas) for water supply on coastal hills
techniques.requires_basis: Fog harvesting works in arid coastal ranges with frequent advective fog, generally below about 1,200 m. The rule cannot see fog frequency itself (see adaptation notes).
techniques.documented_effect: Discusses fog collection's role in water planning for developing countries, drawing on the Chungungo project in northern Chile.
techniques.evidence_source: Schemenauer, R.S. & Cereceda, P. (1994). Fog collection's role in water planning for developing countries. Natural Resources Forum 18(2): 91–100.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Only where persistent fog meets ridges; fog frequency is not in the feature vector, so it must be checked locally before building.

techniques.technique: Drip irrigation of avocado and table grape planted on steep hillsides
techniques.requires_basis: Hillside planting uses cold-air drainage for frost protection on otherwise unusable slopes in arid valleys.
techniques.documented_effect: not available (no verified source linked for this entry)
techniques.evidence_source: INIA Chile extension material (no specific trial report linked).
techniques.adaptation_notes: Hillside planting on bare slopes can increase erosion; needs pressure-compensating emitters and pumping to height.

techniques.technique: Quesungual slash-and-mulch agroforestry (no burning, pruned trees, permanent mulch)
techniques.requires_basis: Developed for sub-humid, frost-free tropical hillsides with a pronounced dry season, where burning and erosion degrade soils.
techniques.documented_effect: Studies soil macrofauna in agricultural landscapes dominated by the Quesungual slash-and-mulch agroforestry system in western Honduras.
techniques.evidence_source: Pauli, N., Barrios, E., Conacher, A.J. & Oberthür, T. (2011). Soil macrofauna in agricultural landscapes dominated by the Quesungual Slash-and-Mulch Agroforestry System, western Honduras. Applied Soil Ecology 47: 119–132.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Requires native tree regrowth to be present and community agreements against burning.

techniques.technique: Area exclosures: degraded hillsides closed to grazing and cutting for regeneration
techniques.requires_basis: Exclosures target degraded, steep communal land unsuitable for cropping.
techniques.documented_effect: Studies sediment deposition and soil development within exclosures in the Tigray highlands.
techniques.evidence_source: Descheemaeker, K. et al. (2006). Sediment deposition and pedogenesis in exclosures in the Tigray highlands, Ethiopia. Geoderma 132: 291–314.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Only works with community by-laws and an alternative feed source (cut-and-carry) for livestock.

techniques.technique: Stone bunds, check dams and percolation trenches at catchment scale
techniques.requires_basis: Catchment-scale soil and water conservation targets sloping cropland in semi-arid to sub-humid highlands.
techniques.documented_effect: Evaluates the impact of soil and water conservation measures on the hydrological response of a catchment in north Ethiopia.
techniques.evidence_source: Nyssen, J. et al. (2010). Impact of soil and water conservation measures on catchment hydrological response — a case in north Ethiopia. Hydrological Processes 24: 1880–1895.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Mass mobilisation built these in the source region; bunds need annual repair and stones available on site.

techniques.technique: Deficit irrigation of tree crops at drought-tolerant stages
techniques.requires_basis: Deficit irrigation presumes irrigation control in a dry climate.
techniques.documented_effect: Reviews deficit irrigation as a strategy for reducing agricultural water use, including crop responses and conditions under which it is viable.
techniques.evidence_source: Fereres, E. & Soriano, M.A. (2007). Deficit irrigation for reducing agricultural water use. Journal of Experimental Botany 58: 147–159.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Pistachio and olive tolerate stage-specific deficit well; many annual crops do not.

techniques.technique: Crop and cultivar selection by salt tolerance (threshold EC) for saline soils and water
techniques.requires_basis: Salinity problems concentrate in irrigated drylands, where evaporation exceeds rainfall leaching.
techniques.documented_effect: FAO water-quality guidance tabulates crop salt tolerance (yield-decline thresholds) for matching crops to saline conditions.
techniques.evidence_source: Ayers, R.S. & Westcot, D.W. (1985). Water quality for agriculture. FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 29 Rev. 1. Rome: FAO.
techniques.adaptation_notes: Measure soil ECe and water EC; tolerance tables assume good drainage and steady-state leaching.
